title: Fibre associated points are detected on a surjective etale scheme atlas
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to Y$ have scheme base $Y$, be of finite type and quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact), with finite type as in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $M$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], meaning locally finitely generated on etale scheme charts. Let $p:T\to X$ be a representable surjective etale morphism with $T$ a scheme, and let $N=p^*M$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. On each scheme chart regard quasi-coherent etale modules as Zariski modules via [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. For $y\in Y$ form $p_y:T_y\to X_y$ by sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Use the topology on space points [def-a1-space-point-topology] and the chartwise relative assassin [def-sfb-space-universal-relative-purity], with scheme associated points [def-trf-relative-assassin]. Then for every $t\in T_y$ one has $t\in\operatorname{Ass}_{T_y}(N_y)$ if and only if $p_y(t)\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(M_y)$, and $p_y(\operatorname{Ass}_{T_y}(N_y))=\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(M_y)$.

source.place: Tags 0CUZ (lemma-relative-assassin), equivalence of conditions (3), (4), (6) and final associated-point clause, and 0CUY (lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-Noetherian-fibres); the exact image assertion is used in the proof of 0CVV (lemma-relative-assassin-constructible).

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $C\to X$. The chart test for finite type, with the identity chart of the scheme $Y$, makes $C\to Y$ locally of finite type. Its scheme fibre $C_y$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(y)$ by scheme base change. A field is Noetherian (its ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so $C_y$ is locally Noetherian. Base change makes $C_y\to X_y$ surjective etale. For any etale scheme chart $a:U\to X_y$, the common refinement $D=C_y\times_{X_y}U$ is a scheme; $D\to C_y$ is etale and $D\to U$ is surjective etale. An etale scheme map is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type: the finitely many polynomial variables in its affine presentation generate the algebra. Thus $D$ is locally Noetherian over $C_y$, and etale-cover descent makes $U$ locally Noetherian. This applies in particular to $T_y$ and to every scheme chart used below; no Noetherian assumption on $Y$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0CUY (lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-Noetherian-fibres); its chartwise proof using Morphisms 01T4 and 01T6, with descent for arbitrary fibre charts.

proof.text: All tensor pullbacks of $M$ used here are quasi-coherent. The scheme etale--Zariski equivalence therefore gives ordinary quasi-coherent modules on $T_y$, on any chart $U\to X_y$, and on their common refinements; its pullback comparison identifies the corresponding scheme pullbacks. The pullbacks along the two composites in a commuting square agree canonically: the tensor-composition isomorphism $P_kP_f\simeq P_{fk}$ of the specified pullbacks [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] has local formula $b\otimes(c\otimes m)\mapsto b\,k^\sharp(c)\otimes m$, with inverse $e\otimes m\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes m)$, and commutes with chart restrictions, so it gives the sheaf comparison for both composites of the square. In particular $N_y=p_y^*M_y$, and for $W=U\times_{X_y}T_y$ with projections $q:W\to U$, $r:W\to T_y$, one has $q^*(a^*M_y)\simeq r^*N_y$. All associated-point tests below consequently use the same Zariski module after pullback.

source.place: Tag 0CUZ (lemma-relative-assassin), pullback notation; Tag 03LC (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial), pullback comparison.

proof.text: If $t\in\operatorname{Ass}_{T_y}(N_y)$, its image belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(M_y)$: $p_y$ is an etale scheme chart by base change, and this chart and $t$ are witnesses in the union-of-chart-images definition of the assassin. The same observation gives the inclusion of the displayed image in the assassin downstairs. Here $B=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ in the purity definition, and for a chart $U\to X_y$ the scheme relative assassin $\operatorname{Ass}_{U/B}$ is the absolute assassin $\operatorname{Ass}_U$, since the fibre of $U\to B$ over the unique point of $B$ is $U$ itself; step 2 identifies the module on the chart $p_y$ with $N_y$.

source.place: Tag 0CV0 (definition-relative-weak-assassin), chart formulation; forward direction of 0CUZ(3)--(4).

proof.text: Conversely suppose $x=p_y(t)\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(M_y)$. By the chartwise definition, choose an etale scheme chart $a:U\to X_y$ and $u\in\operatorname{Ass}_U(a^*M_y)$ with $a(u)=x$. Form $W=U\times_{X_y}T_y$. The scheme-test lemma makes $W$ a scheme and both projections $q:W\to U$, $r:W\to T_y$ etale scheme morphisms. Since $a(u)=p_y(t)$, surjectivity of the map from fibre-product points to compatible point pairs supplies $w\in W$ with $q(w)=u$ and $r(w)=t$. The schemes $U,T_y,W$ are locally Noetherian by step 1 (for $W$, compose either etale projection with its chart). Apply the scheme invariance lemma to $q$ and the quasi-coherent module $a^*M_y$: association of $u$ gives association of $w$ in $q^*a^*M_y$. Step 2 identifies this with $r^*N_y$. Apply the same lemma to $r$ and $N_y$ to deduce $t\in\operatorname{Ass}_{T_y}(N_y)$. This proves the reverse implication for every lift $t$, not merely existence of an associated lift.

source.place: Tag 0CUZ (lemma-relative-assassin), equivalence of chart conditions (3),(4), with the common-refinement argument written out; flat.tex Tag 05FP and divisors.tex Tag 05AR.

proof.text: For $x\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(M_y)$, surjectivity of $p_y$ on points supplies $t$ with $p_y(t)=x$. The reverse implication just proved makes this lift associated. Hence every such $x$ lies in $p_y(\operatorname{Ass}_{T_y}(N_y))$. Together with step 3 this proves the image equality. If the fibre or module is empty or zero, the same membership arguments give equality of empty sets.

source.place: Tag 0CVV (lemma-relative-assassin-constructible), image equality from the chosen surjective etale chart.

lean.statement: theorem space_fibre_assassin_etale_atlas {X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))} (Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace Y) (_hf : MapIsFiniteType f) (_hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f.hom.hom)) (M : X.QCoh) (_hM : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType M.obj) (T : X.EtaleSite) (_hp : IsSurjective T.obj.hom) (y : Y.left) (Ty : (assassinSchemeFibre Y f y).EtaleSite) (i : Ty.obj.left ⟶ T.obj.left) (_hcart : IsPullback Ty.obj.hom (yoneda.map i) (Limits.pullback.fst f.hom (assassinPointBaseMap Y y).hom).hom T.obj.hom) : (∀ t : Ty.obj.left.left, t ∈ Scheme.Modules.associatedPoints ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i.left).obj ((X.schemeRestriction T).obj M.obj)) ↔ schemePointMap Ty.obj.hom t ∈ relativeAssassin (assassinPointBase Y y) (assassinSchemeFibreToPoint Y f y) ((moduleTensorPullback (enlargedFibreProductFst f (assassinPointBaseMap Y y))).obj M.obj)) ∧ (schemePointMap Ty.obj.hom) '' Scheme.Modules.associatedPoints ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i.left).obj ((X.schemeRestriction T).obj M.obj)) = relativeAssassin (assassinPointBase Y y) (assassinSchemeFibreToPoint Y f y) ((moduleTensorPullback (enlargedFibreProductFst f (assassinPointBaseMap Y y))).obj M.obj)
lean.note: The fibre and its residue-field projection abbreviate the existing sheaf fibre-product construction. The module upstairs is the ordinary fibre pullback of the canonical Zariski restriction of M to the original atlas; downstairs it is the specified tensor pullback to X_y. Both pointwise detection and exact image equality are stated.
